100% pure

Purity isn't an ingredient. It's everything we take out.

Most water brands tell you where theirs comes from. We would rather tell you what isn't in it.

The Pureau process is a three-stage system — filtration, reverse osmosis and biological filtration to 0.2 microns. No chemicals, no ozonation, no UV. The result is water 100 times purer than WHO and Australian FSANZ purity standards.

  1. Chlorine
  2. Fluoride
  3. Bacteria
  4. Heavy metals
  5. Sodium
  6. Trace pharmaceuticals
  7. Pesticides

When it really matters

Some households don't choose Pureau. They need it.

Over nearly forty years, Pureau has become the default where minerals, chlorine and scale get in the way.

  • Supplements and powders

    Mixed with water that has nothing else in it.

  • Infant formula preparation

    A long-standing use among Australian parents. Always follow the formula manufacturer's and NHMRC preparation instructions.

  • CPAP and humidified devices

    Equipment that specifies low-mineral water to avoid deposits in the reservoir.

  • Coffee machines, kettles and irons

    No calcium means no limescale building up inside the appliance.

  • Older Australians

    Extra care about water quality as part of everyday wellbeing.

The Pureau process

Three stages. No chemicals.

If you want the engineering, it's all here.

First stage

Filtration

Removes common contaminants and inorganic materials such as nitrates, using carbon and other media developed over decades to purify and soften the water.

Second stage

Reverse osmosis

Water is forced through membranes at high pressure to remove remaining contaminants down to a micron level.

Third stage

Biological filters

Removes substances down to 0.2 microns as a final security measure. Samples are sent daily to Australian Laboratory Services to verify quality through every production run.

Not all ROs are the same

A home filter and a Pureau plant are different things.

Reverse osmosis is a process, not a guarantee. The result depends entirely on what surrounds the membrane — and most home systems leave out the parts that matter most.

△

The storage tank problem

Most under-bench and benchtop home RO units store purified water in a pressurised rubber bladder tank. Still water sitting in a rubber vessel in a warm cabinet is a known environment for bacterial regrowth. By the time it reaches your glass, the purification has been partially reversed.

△

Filter fatigue goes undetected

Home systems depend on the owner replacing pre-filters every 6 to 12 months. An exhausted carbon pre-filter allows chlorine and organic compounds through to the RO membrane, degrading it from the front. Contaminant rejection rates fall quietly, with no alarm and no visible sign.

△

No biological filtration stage

An RO membrane rejects dissolved solids — it does not filter bacteria. Pureau adds a third stage of biological filtration down to 0.2 microns after the membrane. Most home systems stop at the membrane. That gap is where bacteria live.

△

Stage count is not purity

Some home systems are marketed as 7-stage or 9-stage. In most cases the additional stages are mineral-addition cartridges, alkaline stones or UV lamps — each addressing taste or marketing, not purification. More stages does not mean cleaner water.

△

Cold water cuts performance

RO membrane efficiency drops significantly in cold water — a common condition in Australian winters, particularly in southern states. Rejection rates can fall by 15 to 25 per cent in cold supply water with no indication to the user that the system is underperforming.

△

No independent verification

Pureau sends samples to Australian Laboratory Services daily across every production run. A home RO system has no ongoing third-party testing. What the membrane claims to remove, and what it actually removes on any given day, are two different things without verified data to confirm it.

The real numbers

What a home RO actually produces.

NSF/ANSI 58 — the standard most home RO units are certified to — only requires a unit to demonstrate 75% TDS rejection at test conditions. Real-world performance, with aged membranes and suburban water pressure, falls further. These are established industry and independent research findings.

Contaminant Pureau industrial Home RO — new, well-maintained Home RO — typical real-world

Nitrates99.99%75%As low as 50% (NSF minimum)

Total organic carbon99.99%75–85%55–75%
Bacteria (post-tank)Removed to 0.2µmCan exceed tap waterCan exceed tap water
Independent verificationDaily — ALS labsNoneNone

Sources: NSF International; Water Quality Association; Journal of Membrane Science; University of New South Wales water treatment research. Home RO real-world figures reflect typical consumer-grade systems after 12–24 months of use at suburban mains pressure.

A home RO cannot produce Pureau.

The pressure is not high enough. The pre-treatment beds are not there. The biological filtration stage after the membrane does not exist. The storage tank introduces contamination the membrane just removed. And there is no daily laboratory test to tell you any of this is happening.

Pureau operates at industrial membrane pressures home systems cannot physically reach, through carbon and sand pre-treatment banks, through a three-stage process that ends with biological filtration to 0.2 microns absolute — then sealed, not stored in rubber. Every production run is tested independently. Not occasionally. Every run.
